sentenceSets.sentence: The lengthy tangential discussion consumed the time available for the central question.

answerChoices.reasoning: Circular means going around in loops without progress, but tangential specifically means touching only lightly on the edges; the sentence shows a discussion that wanders away, not repeats itself.
Roundabout means taking a long, indirect route, but it implies still heading toward the destination; tangential goes off to the edges and doesn't return to the central question.
Tedious means boring or long-winded, but the sentence's problem is specifically that the discussion is off-topic and peripheral, not necessarily that it's tiresome in delivery.
Digressive means wandering from the main topic, but tangential more specifically means touching only lightly on related matters, not necessarily wandering into completely unrelated subjects.
Verbose means using excessive words, but the issue here is the topic itself—the peripheral nature of the discussion—not merely the quantity of words.
Superfluous means unnecessary or excessive, but it doesn't capture the specific sense of touching peripherally on related matters rather than hitting the main subject.
Irrelevant means having no bearing on the matter, but tangential suggests touching the edge or periphery, not complete lack of connection.
Convoluted means twisted or complicated, but tangential specifically describes the direction of the discussion away from the center, not its complexity.
Urgent means requiring immediate attention; the sentence shows a discussion that wastes available time, so it has no sense of urgency or pressing importance.
Focused means concentrating on a particular point; the sentence explicitly shows the opposite—a discussion that wanders away from the central question.
Essential means absolutely necessary and central; tangential describes what is peripheral and incidental, which is the opposite of essential.

sentenceSets.sentence: The author's tangential remarks about local folklore added color to the narrative but didn't advance the main plot.

answerChoices.reasoning: Marginal means at the edge or of lesser importance, but tangential more specifically implies touching only lightly or incidentally on a topic, rather than simply being unimportant.
Supplementary means added to complete something, but tangential remarks are more peripheral—they don't complement or complete the main narrative as supplementary material would.

Incidental means occurring as a minor consequence, and while the definition of tangential includes this, in context the sentence emphasizes that the remarks deviate from and don't contribute to the main story.
Parenthetical remarks are set apart from the main text, but tangential implies a sidetrack or peripheral touch, not necessarily something formally set apart.
Ornamental means decorative, but tangential remarks are described as off-topic rather than decorative elements intentionally added for aesthetic enhancement.
Gratuitous means unnecessary or unwarranted, but tangential remarks might be interesting even if off-topic; the focus is on their peripheral relationship, not on whether they're warranted.
Whimsical means playful or fanciful, but the sentence doesn't convey whether the folklore remarks are playful; it emphasizes they're peripheral to the plot.
Extraneous means not essential and coming from outside, but tangential suggests touching the edges of what matters, not being entirely foreign to the narrative.
Fundamental means serving as a base or core; the sentence explicitly shows the remarks don't advance the main plot, so they're not fundamental to the story.
Pivotal means central and crucial, but the sentence shows these remarks add only color and don't advance the central action.
Vital means essential and necessary; the sentence shows the remarks are ancillary, not essential to the narrative's progression.

sentenceSets.sentence: His tangential comment about his daughter's soccer game surprised no one at the corporate board meeting; he always found ways to veer off course.

answerChoices.reasoning: Irrelevant means having no connection to the matter at hand, but tangential suggests the comment touches the edges or has some minimal relation, not zero connection.
Inappropriate means unsuitable for the context, but tangential describes the logical or topical direction of the comment, not whether it's proper for the setting.
Offhand means casual or not carefully planned, but tangential specifically describes the topic's relation to the meeting's purpose, not the tone or manner of delivery.
Frivolous means lacking seriousness or importance, but tangential describes the path of thought away from the central subject, not the degree of seriousness.
Evasive means attempting to avoid or escape, but tangential means touching peripherally, not necessarily attempting to dodge an issue.
Tangible means concrete and perceivable, but the sentence requires an adjective describing the comment's relation to the meeting's topic, and tangible doesn't fit that need.
Random means without pattern or plan, but tangential describes a specific type of off-topic remark, not necessarily an unpredictable or aimless one.
Superficial means shallow or on the surface, but tangential describes the direction away from the central topic, not the depth of engagement.
Crucial means critically important; the sentence shows the comment was off-topic and veered away from important business, not contributing crucial insights.
Pertinent means directly relevant to the matter in question; the sentence shows the opposite—a comment that wandered away from the meeting's agenda.
Coherent means logical and consistent; while the comment might be logically structured, the sentence's point is that it wandered off-topic, not about its logical coherence.
